chunks: He came to Baghdad from Khorasan in the year [408 AH], and he was twenty-three years old.

key_terms.بَغْدَادَ: Baghdad — the Abbasid capital and pre-eminent center of Islamic scholarship in the 5th century AH
key_terms.خُرَاسَانَ: Khorasan — the historical northeastern Iranian region; al-Tusi was born in Tus (near modern Mashhad)
key_terms.سَنَةَ: year — referring to 408 AH, corresponding to approximately 1017 CE

ai.seo_question: When did Sheikh al-Tusi arrive in Baghdad and how old was he when he emigrated from Khorasan?
ai.summary: This brief biographical note records the arrival of Sheikh al-Tusi (Sheikh al-Ta'ifa) in Baghdad from Khorasan in 408 AH (c. 1017 CE) at the age of twenty-three. This journey marks the beginning of his formal scholarly training in Baghdad under luminaries such as Sheikh al-Mufid, setting him on the path to becoming the foremost jurist and hadith scholar of the Shia tradition.
